about.title: About Me
about.content:
If you already know me, you know my name is Lucas Alvarenga, but many people also call me Alvarenga! I am a Senior Mobile Software Engineer with 5+ years of experience, focused on Android and the evolution of large-scale digital products. My work brings together software architecture, modularization, quality, integrations, and user experience. I also connect software engineering and AI through Spec-Driven Development, context engineering, and AI-assisted development in real engineering workflows.

I started programming at the age of 13, specifically with Android, using Java back in 2017. As I was about to enter high school, I wanted to study at a technical school. The following year, I enrolled at Rezende Rammel to take an IT course. It was three incredible years where I deepened my knowledge, especially in Java and later in Kotlin. Additionally, I had contact with other languages such as JavaScript, PHP, C, and Pascal, as well as frameworks like React.js and Flutter.

In 2020, I decided to pursue a career as an Android developer. I went through several selection processes and interviews until I landed my first internship, and within just three months, I was hired. Since August 2019, I have also been creating technology content and documenting my journey from student to software developer.

carrer.title: Career
carrer.description: Below is a summary of my resume, professional experience, and education.

experience1.title: Senior Mobile Software Engineer | AI Ambassador
experience1.list: Contributed to mobile initiatives that supported over 1,300% growth in product adoption | Implemented A/B tests in key journeys to validate UX hypotheses and support data-informed decisions | Introduced Spec-Driven Development with OpenSpec and created a reusable Harness workflow for AI-assisted development | Support teams adopting SDD, context engineering, and effective LLM use | Applied AI to production work, including technical documentation, Android flows, API integrations, and A/B tests

experience2.title: Android Software Engineer
experience2.list: Developed a centralized experience for viewing and managing automatic payments | Evolved the Android architecture with MVVM and modularization, and contributed to the gradual migration of XML screens to Jetpack Compose | Increased automated test coverage from 14% to 80.5% with JUnit 4 and MockK | Partnered with Product and Design on user journeys, accessibility, and user experience | Helped automate 21 Android scenarios with Robot Framework and Appium, and documented test execution and maintenance

experience3.title: Android Software Engineer
experience3.list: Contributed to restructuring the Android app with MVVM and modularization | Created automated tests with JUnit 5 and MockK | Helped document Android standards and best practices | Contributed to architecture decisions and onboarding new developers | Integrated REST APIs and took part in Design and Discovery processes

experience4.title: Junior Android Developer
experience4.list: Built features with Product and Android teams | Refactored and applied MVVM and Clean Architecture | Wrote unit tests with JUnit 5 and MockK | Contributed to modularization, REST API and Zendesk integrations | Helped onboard new developers

experience5.title: Android Developer Intern
experience5.list: Built features and fixed bugs in the Gerentes Digitais app | Worked with Firebase, Retrofit, and Android Jetpack libraries | Integrated image loading with Picasso and Glide

oddword.description: One secret word. One person pretending to know it. And a group trying to catch the bluff.
oddword.availability: Coming soon to Android and iOS
oddword.heroAlt: Who is the infiltrator? game home screen
oddword.howDescription: The phone goes around. The mystery stays.
oddword.step1: Everyone secretly receives the same word, except one person: they find out they are the infiltrator.
oddword.step2: Give clues without saying the word. The infiltrator must pretend to know it and blend into the conversation.
oddword.step3: Decide as a group who the infiltrator is. Then reveal the answer in the app.
oddword.step4: If the infiltrator is caught, the majority scores. If they get away, they earn points.
oddword.featuresEyebrow: THINGS ARE ABOUT TO GET SUSPICIOUS
oddword.feature1Description: Pass the phone around to reveal each player's role. No sign-up or internet connection needed.
oddword.feature2Description: Choose a category and set the conversation timer for your group.
oddword.feature3Description: Track points after every round and see who reads the clues best.
